page.title: SAM2 vs SAM3 Frozen Feature Clustering for Binary Texture Partitioning

coarse_only.takeaway: SAM2 wins coarse-only parity cleanly on RWTD.
CAID shows a clear SAM2 lead in coarse-only parity.
This is the largest same-flavor margin on the page.

flip_averaged.takeaway: RWTD flip-avg remains the one place where SAM3 still holds a small edge.
CAID flip-avg is close, but SAM2 still edges ahead.
SAM2 keeps a clear flip-avg lead on STLD.

stories.title: RWTD: SAM2 Wins the Coarse-Only Parity Check
stories.summary: On this tile-and-grout crop, the same-flavor coarse-only comparison is visually clear. SAM2 coarse tracks the diagonal split cleanly, while SAM3 coarse breaks the scene into broad horizontal bands.

stories.title: STLD: Coarse-Only Still Favors SAM2 Decisively
stories.summary: This compact synthetic foreground is representative of the coarse-only gap on STLD. SAM2 coarse recovers the object cleanly, while SAM3 coarse overfills a much larger false-positive region.

stories.title: STLD: Flip-Averaged Parity Still Favors SAM2
stories.summary: The thin oblique strip is harder, but the same-flavor flip-avg comparison still separates the models. SAM2 flip captures far more of the structure, while SAM3 flip nearly collapses the signal.

stories.title: RWTD: Flip-Averaged Is the Main Exception
stories.summary: RWTD flip-avg is the one same-flavor slice where SAM3 keeps a slight aggregate lead. This crop is included as a useful counterexample rather than hidden by the summary.
